records.title: Omega-3 Fatty Acids — Health Professional Fact Sheet
records.publisher: National Institutes of Health, Office of Dietary Supplements
records.public_summary: A federal reference for omega-3 forms, dietary sources, intake context, biomarker considerations, safety, and the limits of current evidence.
records.scope: General omega-3 education for health professionals; it does not evaluate or endorse a specific product or testing service.
records.limitations: The page is broad reference material. Individual studies and qualified claims still require context, and it does not establish personal need or treatment advice.
records.rights_evidence: Stable public NIH HTTPS page; this manifest links to the source and uses an original summary without reproducing source text.

records.title: Vitamin D — Health Professional Fact Sheet
records.publisher: National Institutes of Health, Office of Dietary Supplements
records.public_summary: A federal reference covering vitamin D sources, intake guidance, status assessment, deficiency risk, safety, and research across health outcomes.
records.scope: General vitamin D education and laboratory-context background; it does not interpret an individual result or endorse a supplement.
records.limitations: Population guidance cannot determine an individual dose or explain a result without clinical context, and evidence varies by outcome.
records.rights_evidence: Stable public NIH HTTPS page; this manifest links to the source and uses an original summary without reproducing source text.

records.title: Probiotics: Usefulness and Safety
records.publisher: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health
records.public_summary: A federal overview of probiotic terminology, studied uses, strain-specific uncertainty, safety considerations, and limits in the evidence base.
records.scope: General education about probiotics and research uncertainty; it does not establish that one commercial formulation will produce another formulation’s results.
records.limitations: Effects can depend on strain, formulation, population, and outcome. Safety evidence is more limited for vulnerable populations and long-term use.
records.rights_evidence: Stable public NCCIH HTTPS page; NCCIH identifies the publication as public-domain information, while this site still uses an original summary.

records.title: Hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) Test
records.publisher: MedlinePlus, U.S. National Library of Medicine
records.public_summary: A consumer-oriented federal explanation of what an HbA1c test measures, why it may be ordered, and how results are discussed in clinical care.
records.scope: General laboratory education. It provides context for the measurement rather than validating a particular home collection kit or interpreting a personal result.
records.limitations: Interpretation can be affected by health conditions and clinical context; visitors should use their clinician and laboratory report for personal decisions.
records.rights_evidence: Stable public MedlinePlus HTTPS page; this manifest links to the source and uses an original summary without reproducing source text.

records.scope: Regulatory and label-literacy context for U.S. dietary supplements; it is not a quality rating and does not establish product efficacy.
records.limitations: The guide contains nonbinding recommendations and must be read alongside current statutes, regulations, and later FDA updates.

records.limitations: Claim requirements depend on wording, evidence, product category, and current law; the page is not a substitute for product-specific review.
